--- title: "Household Location Burden Index" subtitle: "Scoping document — for review, only a base scenario exists so far" format: html: toc: true toc-depth: 2 embed-resources: true execute: echo: false warning: false message: false jupyter: july2025 --- **[← All run sets](../../index.qmd)** ## The question This study asks whether the TDM could quantify the additional **Congested Roadway Capacity Demand** — peak-period roadway burden — created by adding a fixed number of typical households (500 or 1000) at different locations around the region. Capturing that burden properly means letting the TDM run its full multimodal, all-day pipeline for those households (mode choice, trip timing, route choice) and measuring the *delay it imposes on everyone else already on the system*, not just the new households' own travel. The result would be expressed as a Burden Index relative to a reference location at the region's geographic center (Murray): a household placed in Western Davis County, for instance, might place meaningfully more burden on the system than one placed in one of Davis County's designated City or Town Centers. ## Decisions needed before building this | Decision | Options | Recommendation | If left unresolved | |---|---|---|---| | **N** — households per site | 500 or 1000 | 1000, for a more clearly measurable effect | Defaults to 500 (boss's first-mentioned number) | | **Congestion threshold** | V/C ≥ 0.8, ≥ 1.0, or report both | Report both — cheap, since both are already in the same summary CSV | Defaults to reporting both | | **Peak window** | AM+PM only, or all four periods | AM+PM, matching "peak-period" in the original ask; MD/EV available in the same file if wanted later | Defaults to AM+PM | | **Site list** | See "Candidate sites" below — Murray control (1619), Western Davis typical (684 or 602), Davis CTC (674, 610, 600, or 780) | Murray 1619 + Syracuse typical 684 + Syracuse City Center 674, for the minimal 3-scenario proof-of-methodology build | Build proceeds with the recommended picks below unless told otherwise | | **Network vintage(s)** | 2023 (today) only, or 2023 + 2055 (long-range Needs) | Both — burden today, plus whether the center-vs-sprawl gap holds, widens, or narrows as the region grows to its 2055 forecast. More relevant to a growth-siting decision than a single-year snapshot | Proposed as part of the initial build, not a later add-on | : {tbl-colwidths="[20,30,30,20]" .fixed-table} ## Proposed methodology **Design:** one **Base** run, one **Control** run (Base + N households added at a Murray TAZ — the geographic-center reference), and one **Test** run per candidate site (Base + the same N households added at that site's TAZ). Same household count everywhere, so differences reflect *location*, not household mix. **Run this whole pattern twice — once against 2023 (today), once against 2055 (long-range Needs)**, proposed as part of the initial build rather than a later add-on (see "Decisions needed" above). The diagram below shows one vintage; the 2055 pass is the identical pattern against the 2055 network and 2055 SE forecast instead. ```{mermaid} flowchart LR SE["Base SE data
(2023 or 2055)"] --> Base["Base run
no HH added"] SE -->|"+N HH at Murray"| Control["Control run"] SE -->|"+N HH at Site A"| SiteA["Test: Site A"] SE -->|"+N HH at Site B"| SiteB["Test: Site B"] SE -->|"+N HH at Site ..."| SiteN["Test: Site ..."] Base --> Metric["Delta VHT = Test minus Base
peak periods, congested V/C tiers"] Control --> Metric SiteA --> Metric SiteB --> Metric SiteN --> Metric Metric --> Index["Burden Index(site) =
Delta VHT(site) / Delta VHT(Murray control)"] ``` **Metric:** systemwide congested vehicle-hours-traveled (ΔVHT), not just the new households' own trips — the whole point is capturing the delay imposed on *everyone else*, which only shows up as a regionwide before/after difference. Peak periods (AM, PM), filtered to links at or above a congestion threshold (V/C ≥ 0.8 and/or ≥ 1.0). **Burden Index** = ΔVHT(site) ÷ ΔVHT(Murray control) — giving the "1.6x" / "1.2x" style figure directly, computed separately for 2023 and 2055 so the two years can be compared side by side. ::: {.callout-note} ## A caveat on comparing 2023 and 2055 directly N households is a much bigger *relative* bump against a TAZ's 2023 household count than against its 2055 forecast, which already assumes decades of organic growth at these sites. A rising or falling Burden Index between the two years could partly reflect that shrinking relative size, not just a real shift in how the network absorbs growth at that location — worth calling out when the results are reported, not something the study design itself corrects for. ::: ## Baseline signal, from the registered `base` scenario These are real numbers from an already-completed model run — not simulated for illustration. That run is the region's current (2023) road network exactly as it exists today, with no new households added yet; reusing it here meant no new traffic-model run was needed just to produce this table. It shows how congested the road network already is, by time of day, using the same "how congested" math (V/C ≥ 0.8 and ≥ 1.0 — road segments running at or above 80%/100% of their capacity) that will measure each candidate site's impact later. ::: {#baseline-table .cell execution_count=2} | Period | Total VHT | VHT at V/C ≥ 0.8 | VHT at V/C ≥ 1.0 | |---|---:|---:|---:| | AM | 225,355 | 66,522 (29.5%) | 17,225 (7.6%) | | MD | 405,888 | 43,243 (10.7%) | 908 (0.2%) | | PM | 338,003 | 146,780 (43.4%) | 51,135 (15.1%) | | EV | 312,990 | 115 (0.0%) | 0 (0.0%) | Regionwide lane-miles in this network: **9,014** (segment-direction rows). ::: This is *system scale*, not the site-comparison metric itself — it's today's regionwide congested-VHT backdrop that a 500–1000-household ΔVHT would be measured against. PM is the most congested period by a wide margin; AM is a distant second; MD and EV carry almost no V/C≥1.0 congestion. This confirms AM+PM is the right peak-period scope for the Burden Index, and suggests PM alone may show the clearest site-to-site differences. ::: {.callout-note} ## What's still missing for Control/Test scenarios This `base` scenario only has the segment summary curated so far — the regionwide *congestion-tier* summary (`Summary_HighwayNet.csv`, needed for the Δ calculation once Control/Test scenarios exist) requires the custom driver-script edit described below, then re-registering `base` with that output included too. A 2055 counterpart to this `base` scenario doesn't exist yet either — it needs the same one-step `import-manual-run` registration against the `v10.0-beta.2` run set's already-run `Needs_2055` scenario, no new Cube Voyager run required (see "How this fits the run-management framework" below). Adding Control/Test scenarios for either year still needs real Cube Voyager runs — see "Decisions needed" and "Effort and runtime" below. ::: ## Candidate sites ::: {.callout-note} Candidates, not yet confirmed. Data-driven, but the final pick is a decision for the study lead — see "Decisions needed" above. ::: Method: spatially joined the TDM's own TAZ shapefile (`tdm/1_Inputs/1_TAZ/WFv1000_TAZ.shp`) against WFRC's **Wasatch Choice 2050 Centers (Vision Map)** feature service — the actual regional-centers layer referenced in the original ask, queried live from `services1.arcgis.com/taguadKoI1XFwivx/.../Wasatch_Choice_2050_Centers_(Vision_Map)/FeatureServer` — then cross-referenced household counts from `SE_2023.csv`. Household/city figures below are pulled live from those same local files on every render. ::: {#cell-candidate-sites-map .cell execution_count=3} ::: {#candidate-sites-map .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {#candidate-sites-table .cell execution_count=4} | Candidate | TAZID | City | HH | Pop | Note | |---|---:|---|---:|---:|---| | Murray control | 1619 | Murray | 1,440 | 2,663 | Populous, ordinary residential TAZ -- geographic-center reference | | Western Davis -- typical (recommended) | 684 | Syracuse | 751 | 2,511 | Large low-density subdivision, no designated center nearby | | Western Davis -- typical (alternate) | 602 | West Point | 404 | 1,747 | Further west by X-coordinate; smaller sample | | Davis CTC -- Syracuse City Center (recommended) | 674 | Syracuse | 398 | 1,367 | Same city as the recommended typical site -- isolates center-vs-not | | Davis CTC -- Clinton Town Center (alternate) | 610 | Clinton | 185 | 626 | | | Davis CTC -- West Point City Center (alternate) | 600 | West Point | 346 | 1,051 | | | Davis CTC -- Station Park, Farmington (alternate, Urban Center) | 780 | Farmington | 301 | 1,130 | Larger/more significant center, for a bigger contrast | ::: **Recommendation:** pair the Syracuse typical site (684) against the Syracuse City Center (674) — same city, so the comparison isolates "designated center vs. not" rather than mixing in city-level differences, which is exactly the contrast the original ask describes. Combined with the Murray control (1619), that's the minimal 3-scenario build (plus `base`) needed to prove the methodology end-to-end before expanding to a fuller site list. ## What the model already gives us to work with This isn't hypothetical — the pieces exist in the TDM today, just not wired together for this purpose: | Need | Existing TDM piece | Status | |---|---|---| | Systemwide VMT/VHT by period, purpose, and congestion tier (V/C ≥ 0.8, ≥ 1.0) | `2_ModelScripts/7_PostProcessing/4_BCA_Summaries/02_Summarize_HighwayNet.s` | Exists, does exactly this — but its `READ FILE` line is **commented out** in the default driver script, so it doesn't currently run | | A way to add households to a specific TAZ without touching anything else | `WFRC_SEFile` / `MAG_SEFile` — plain TAZ-level `TOTHH`/`HHPOP` CSVs | Exists; this framework already has a proven pattern for generating per-scenario SE variants (used for the `non-motorized-2023` study) | | 2023 and 2055 base networks to build on | The `v10.0-beta.2` run set's `Base_2023` and `Needs_2055` scenarios, both already run in this repo | 2023 **done** — registered as this run set's own `base` scenario via `import-manual-run`. 2055 not yet registered, but the same one-step `import-manual-run` against the already-run `Needs_2055` scenario is all it needs | | Household composition (size, income, workers, autos) for the "typical household" | `1_HHDisag_AutoOwn/` (LifeCycle → HHDisaggregation → AutoOwnership) | The model derives this itself from `TOTHH`/`HHPOP`, using distributions that already respond to local accessibility — there's no separate lever to force a specific household profile | : {tbl-colwidths="[35,30,35]" .fixed-table} ## How this fits the run-management framework Mechanically, this is a new run set — `household-location-burden` — following the same pattern already proven by `non-motorized-2023` and `bring-work-trips-closer-to-home`: - **`base`** (2023) — **done**. Registered by reusing the existing `v10.0-beta.2-2023` run rather than re-running full feedback from scratch. To pick up the BCA congestion-tier summary once the driver script is edited, its raw folder can be re-entered via `start_at_label` (resuming just the post-processing steps) rather than a full re-run. - **`base-2055`** — same treatment, reusing `v10.0-beta.2`'s already-run `Needs_2055` scenario. Not yet registered. - **`control-murray-2023`** / **`control-murray-2055`** and one **`site--2023`** / **`site--2055`** pair per candidate location — each pointed at its own generated SE file (drawn from the matching year's SE forecast) via `overrides.WFRC_SEFile`, the same relative-path mechanism `non-motorized-2023` uses. - A shared **custom driver script** (this run set's own copy of `__HailMary_1Subfolder.s`, with the BCA summary line turned on) — the framework's existing `driver_script` mechanism, no core code changes needed. - **Outputs curated**: just the small `Summary_HighwayNet.csv` per scenario — well under the size ceiling, no raw network/matrix files committed. - A small Burden Index calculation module, reported here once real runs exist — same shape as `non-motorized-2023`'s `report_loader.py`. No changes to the TDM codebase, the orchestrator's core logic, or how Cube Voyager runs are required — this is entirely new configuration plus one custom driver script, the same category of work as every other run set in this repo. ## Effort and runtime Each Test/Control scenario needs a **full feedback run** (mode choice logsums + four-period assignment) — households are added before disaggregation, so nothing upstream can be skipped or reused between sites. Only the two Base runs benefit from reuse (both already run, neither needs re-running). Running both the 2023 and 2055 vintages roughly doubles the Test/Control run count for the same site list: N sites × 2 years + 2 control runs, against two free Base runs. Runtime scales linearly with number of sites *and* years; `max_parallel_runs` (already supported, not yet exercised on a real multi-scenario batch) could help once Cube Voyager licensing/hardware limits on this workstation are confirmed. **Why not combine multiple sites into one run?** Congestion is non-linear — that's the whole reason V/C-tiered VHT is the metric. Adding households from two sites in the same run gives you their *combined* effect on network delay, with no way to split credit between them afterward (their trips might stack on the same congested links, or might not interact at all). Base and Control aren't combinable either — they're mutually exclusive states of the same synthetic population. Recovering true per-site effects from combined runs would need a full factorial design (every combination, solved for interaction terms), which needs *more* runs than one-at-a-time, not fewer. So N candidate sites need N separate Test runs against one shared Base — this design is already the minimal N+1, and the +1 is free (Base is reused, not re-run). Suggested build order: 1. Confirm the Base-run reuse strategy and the driver-script edit; validate `Summary_HighwayNet.csv` comes out as expected on the existing 2023 Base run alone. 2. Register `base-2055` the same way, and confirm it too. 3. Build SE generation + one real site + the Murray control for **2023 only**; validate the ΔVHT / Burden Index math end-to-end on real output before committing to the full site list or the second year. 4. Once proven, replicate that same site + control for **2055**, to confirm the pattern holds across both vintages. 5. Add the remaining sites from the confirmed list, for both years. ## Bottom line The metric, the SE-modification mechanism, and the run-set framework are all already proven in this repo for other studies — this is a matter of configuration and one small driver-script change, not new engineering. Every remaining decision above (N, congestion threshold, peak window, final site picks, network vintages) has a sensible default, so the build can proceed on the recommended picks — 2023 and 2055, both — unless told otherwise.
